pattern.crimePattern: a boda rider about to lose his motorbike to the lender kills her on the ride home, then claims he dropped her at her gate
pattern.notes: Fictional people, laga, shop and lender. The swept yard is the absence: a broom pattern that nobody crossed. Three liars: the killer, his guarantor (false alibi) and the shop assistant (a small theft unrelated to the killing).

ob.text: A water vendor reports a woman dead under a thorn bush in the dry Kawalase laga on the edge of Lodwar town: Akai Lotukoi (31), who runs a mobile-money shop.

facts.text: Akai Lotukoi was found dead under a thorn bush in the Kawalase laga on Sunday morning.
Akai was strangled with a broad, flat strap. Her cash bag is gone; her phone is in her pocket.
Her scarf is soft cotton, about 1 cm wide when folded, still around her shoulders.
Ewoi: one boda came along the laga track with a passenger, stopped and stood; scuffed ground; her shoes two steps from the bike; one rider left alone. Last evening.
A black rubber boda luggage strap, about 3 cm wide, was flung into a thorn bush 50 m down the laga, on the bike's line out.
The broom pattern in the yard is unbroken from the gate to Akai's door this morning.
Napeyo: "I swept at six like every day. I went to bed at ten thinking she'd gone to a friend. In the morning my pattern was perfect. Nobody came in."
Napeyo: Akai and her ex-husband Ekeno fought over the children's school fees.
Napeyo sat with neighbours in the compound from 18:00 to 22:00.
Mary: Akai closed at half past seven; Dennis, a boda rider she lends to, was waiting at the door to give her a lift home "to talk".
Mary: Akai carried her loan ledger and the day's cash home in her cash bag every night.
The float book against the agent statement: cash short KSh 6,500 over two weeks, a few hundred at a time.
Choir mistress: the choir collected Mary at the shop door at 19:30 and she sang with them until 21:30.
There is no luggage strap on Dennis's rack; it was seen on Saturday afternoon tying a sack of charcoal for a customer.
Chairman: every rider at the stage keeps a rubber strap on the rack.
The stage file: Dennis borrowed KSh 220,000 from Akai for his motorbike and repaid KSh 40,000. Akai's Friday note: "Repossess Monday. Guarantor: K. Nyakundi."
Chairman Ekai: Dennis got back to the stage at about 20:15, on his own.
Chairman Ekai: Kevin was at the stage from 18:00 until late; the other riders agree.
Records: Akai's last transaction was the closing float report at 19:28.
Records: Dennis called Kevin at 20:09, for 40 seconds.
Under Dennis's mattress: Akai's cash bag with KSh 64,200.
In Dennis's room: Akai's loan ledger with his page torn out, and the page burned in a tin.
In Dennis's room: a new rubber strap still in its wrapper, bought this morning at 07:30.
Bus manifest: Ekeno left on the 18:00 bus to Kakuma and signed into a Kakuma lodging at 21:40.
Fingerprints taken from Dennis in detention.
Post-mortem: strangulation with a flat strap about 3 cm wide, with a moulded ridged pattern in the mark. No head injury, no wound.
Post-mortem: death on Saturday between 19:30 and 20:30.
Lab: the strap's moulded ridges match the ligature mark; Akai's hair is caught in the buckle.
Lab: Dennis's fingerprints on the clasp of Akai's cash bag.
Missing: there are no footprints or boda tracks in her swept yard.
Missing: her loan book is missing.
Missing: there are no signs of a struggle at the shop.
Missing: his luggage strap is missing.
Missing: her cash bag is missing.

Dennis: "I asked her to give me time. She said Monday. I didn't mean to... I don't want to say any more."

reconstruction.text: Dennis bought his motorbike on a KSh 220,000 loan from Akai and paid KSh 40,000 in eight months. On Friday she wrote to the stage chairman: repossess Monday; guarantor K. Nyakundi.
Saturday, 18:00. Napeyo sweeps the yard, as every evening. At 19:28 Akai sends her closing float report. Dennis is waiting at the door and offers her a lift home, "to talk".
On the laga track, out of sight of the road, he stops and asks her to tear up his page. She refuses. He pulls the rubber strap off his rack and strangles her.
He takes her cash bag and ledger, flings the strap into a thorn bush and rides back. At 20:09 he calls Kevin: "If anyone asks, I was with you from quarter to eight." He reaches the stage at 20:15.
That night he tears his page out and burns it in a tin. On Sunday morning he buys a new strap. In the yard, Napeyo's broom lines lie unbroken until dawn.

clockPlan.note: Two stamps: records on both lines and a warrant on Dennis's room. Detain Dennis after the search; prints (6 h + 4) and the strap match (12 h + 4) come back inside 24 h.

ui.beatNotes: Reading a swept yard. The yard photo shows Napeyo's broom pattern as fine curved lines; the player drags Dennis's claimed route ("at the gate, walked to the door") onto it and the line glows red where it would have had to break the pattern.
